title: Windows Hub loses archive paths passed to PowerShell
original_report: On Windows with Hobbyka Hub 0.4.26, install onec-direct-cli fails because PowerShell 5.1 receives empty positional arguments for ZIP listing and extraction.
discovery_scope: plugins/hobbyka-hub/bin/hobbyka-hub.mjs archive listing, extraction, and creation
expected: Hub validates the downloaded ZIP paths, extracts the plugin, and completes installation.
actual: ZipFile.OpenRead receives an empty path and Node then fails to open the missing .entries file.
environment: Reported on Windows, PowerShell 5.1, Node.js 24.19.0, Hobbyka Hub 0.4.26; focused regression and archive lifecycle verified on macOS.
reproduction: A focused source regression test requires every Windows archive operation to use the system tar.exe path and rejects the broken PowerShell positional-argument pattern.
failure_signal: The focused test exits 1 because Hub 0.4.26 still invokes powershell.exe with $args after -Command.
root_cause: Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not bind the trailing process arguments to $args as the Hub command strings assumed. Listing, extraction, and ZIP creation shared the broken pattern.
fix_summary: Use Windows' built-in tar.exe for ZIP listing, extraction, and creation while preserving path validation before extraction.
why_causal: The fix removes the failed PowerShell argument boundary entirely; the same tar listing and extraction already completed the reported Windows user path on a temporary copy.

reproduction_files.summary: Focused regression for all Windows archive operations.

fix_files.summary: Replace PowerShell ZIP operations with tar.exe.

checks.name: Focused regression
checks.detail: The same test changed from exit 1 to exit 0.

checks.name: Archive lifecycle
checks.detail: Created, listed, and extracted a ZIP with the same tar argument structure.

limitations: The final released binary still requires confirmation on Valera's original Windows installation command.
residual_risks: A Windows image without the inbox tar.exe tool would fail explicitly at process launch; the reported Windows environment already demonstrated tar.exe.
notes: The existing isSafeEntry validation still runs before every extraction.
